# QDOJO — combat implementation briefing

Updated 2026-09-21. UNSIGNED working document. Any signature/hash covering
the old riddle briefing does not cover this text. The old copy is preserved
at docs/archive/riddle-v0/apps/web/llms.txt in the repository.

qdojo is pivoting to autonomous combat. Current executable code remains the
legacy riddle game until the implementation milestones are complete.
Do not tell an owner the existing ./dojo launcher already starts combat.

Read repository docs/spec.md, combat.md, protocol.md, matchmaking.md,
competition.md, api.md, npcs.md, model.md and pivot-plan.md, in that order.
The repository's GPT6_HANDOFF.md is the current implementation handoff.

Three rounds per fight, six simultaneous actions per round; health/resources
carry between rounds. Both bots commit before revealing. Resolve from the
exact matrix and numbered rules. A series contains separate fresh fights.
No house answer, solve-speed winner or random damage roll exists in combat.

Bots run on their owners' machines. NPCs, including random-v1, use the same
observation/action interface. Free practice needs no wallet/NFT. Disclosed
house NPCs cannot inflate ranked wins or season qualification.

Keep spending decisions separate from plan selection. Fail closed before entry
if configuration, strategy, funds or chain state cannot be read. Never expose
keys or unrevealed plan salts; persist exact plan and salt before commitment.
Don't replace a plan after commit. Don't send live transactions, publish docs,
mint assets or deploy just because a development specification exists.

For the code that exists today, this read-only help command is valid:

```sh
uv run qdojo bot --help
```

Combat commands listed in docs/api.md are planned interfaces until implemented.
Keep legacy records and finance separate. Preserve the arcade style, drive
combat animation from confirmed traces and report verification scope honestly.
